kept.claim: The reply-to username link color in `.topic-meta-data h5 a` changed from lightness 30% to 70% for light themes, making it much fainter than before.
kept.body:
## [ISSUE] Light-theme color for `.topic-meta-data h5 a` changed from 30% to 70%

**Severity:** MEDIUM — visible regression in default light theme: bold username links become pale gray

### The Problem
Before:
```scss
color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%);
```
After (line 291):
```scss
color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%));
```
The light-theme argument is now 70%, not the original 30%, and the dark-theme argument is 30% instead of the mirrored 70%. Both values look like they were swapped.

### Theory / Proof
`dark-light-choose($light, $dark)` (app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/variables.scss:46) returns `$light` whenever `brightness($primary) < brightness($secondary)`, i.e. for every default/light color scheme. The PR's stated intent (title: "scale-color $lightness must use $secondary for dark themes") is a pure refactor for light themes: the first argument should be the exact original `scale-color($primary, $lightness: N%)` and the second the mirrored `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: (100-N)%)`. Every other one of the ~115 replacements in this PR follows that N / 100-N rule.

### What happens today vs. what will break
On any light scheme, `dark-light-choose` returns the first argument, so this link goes from dark gray (30%) to light gray (70%): a clear contrast drop on white. On dark schemes, it gets `$secondary` at 30%, much darker than the intended 70%, so it's also low-contrast there.

### Research
Sass `scale-color($c, $lightness: N%)` moves lightness N% of the way toward white (Sass docs, color.scale). So 30% and 70% are very different results: on a black `$primary`, 30% gives ~#4d4d4d and 70% gives ~#b3b3b3. The mirrored dark-theme value for original N is `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 100-N%)`, which is the convention used by every other replacement in this diff.

### Recommendation
```scss
color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%));
```
kept.evidence: desktop/topic-post.scss:291 old 30% -> new (70%,30%); dark-light-choose (variables.scss:46-52) returns first arg on light themes; all other conversions keep original light value and mirror (100-N).

Light themes lose the name/title visual hierarchy on the groups member list; dark themes get 50% instead of 70%.

### Research
Sass `scale-color($c, $lightness: N%)` moves lightness N% of the way toward white (Sass docs, color.scale). So 30% and 70% are very different results: on a black `$primary`, 30% gives ~#4d4d4d and 70% gives ~#b3b3b3.
